candidates.computation_change_reason: Hardness-dependent acute/chronic dissolved WQC formulas and their pre-calculated numeric values both appear; different choices of hardness, formula evaluation, or whether to use the formula versus the tabulated number would change the applicable enforceable limit for Chromium III.

Lead limits depend on separate hardness-based correction factors (CF3/CF4) in addition to the base exponential formulas; interpretation of how CF3/CF4 are applied or which hardness value is used would change the computed acute and chronic limits.

Copper acute and chronic dissolved limits are hardness-dependent with different exponents; alternative hardness inputs or formula-versus-tabulated-value interpretation would change which numeric limit applies for compliance comparison.

The table header specifies dissolved-form water quality criteria in micrograms per liter; interpreting whether reported total versus dissolved measurements, or different unit conversions, are comparable to these limits would change exceedance determinations.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Multiple parallel limit columns (acute aquatic as 2.13*Ce, domestic supply, chronic aquatic, human health, irrigation, wildlife, and TMDL) are presented; which column constitutes the enforceable permit limit for a given parameter and monitoring context would change applicable-limit and exceedance computations.

The (P) designation, MQL of 60, blank ambient/effluent cells, numeric human-health criterion of 640, and 1E+100 placeholders in other columns create ambiguity about whether an enforceable numeric limit exists, which criterion applies, and whether monitoring for this parameter is obligated.

Arsenic has populated ambient/effluent concentrations driving calculated instream limits alongside multiple distinct criteria columns (e.g., 0.03196253 chronic aquatic versus 9 human health); interpretation of (P), which limit governs, and whether effluent-derived values are operative would change limit applicability and monitoring-obligation evaluation.

Three separate chromium entries (III, VI, and undifferentiated dissolved) carry different acute/chronic criteria and placeholder values; which row applies to a given reported chromium measurement (speciated versus total dissolved) would change the selected enforceable limit.

Blank ambient and effluent concentration cells coexist with zero instream-calculated columns and a domestic criterion of 2000 versus 1E+100 elsewhere; interpreting blanks as no applicable effluent limit, as missing data, or as triggering a different criterion column would change both limit applicability and missing-evidence classification.

This row reports ambient and effluent concentrations in mg/l while most metals use ug/l, and yields multiple calculated instream limits plus a wildlife criterion of 132; unit handling and selection among acute, chronic, and wildlife columns would change the applicable numeric limit.

Residual chlorine shows distinct numeric acute aquatic (11 and 19 in different columns) and wildlife (11) criteria amid 1E+100 placeholders; which aquatic column is enforceable and whether the 1.00E+100 domestic entry is a limit or sentinel would change compliance comparison.

Method quantitation limits are listed per parameter; interpreting whether results below MQL are non-detects, unreportable for compliance comparison, or evidence of adequate monitoring affects both whether a numeric limit comparison is performed and how missing or low-level results are classified.

The value 1E+100 appears repeatedly across criteria columns; treating it as no numeric limit, as a non-operative placeholder, or as a literal cap would change whether enforceable comparisons apply and whether absence of a numeric criterion implies conditional non-requirement versus unresolved applicability.
